Class Board

java.lang.Object
chess.model.Board
public class Board extends Object
The 8 x 8 grid of squares and the record of captured pieces.

The board stores pieces in a Piece[8][8] array indexed by [row][col] using the mapping documented in Position. An empty square holds null.

The board knows where pieces are but not whose turn it is or whether a move is legal; those decisions belong to Game. The board's invariant is that every non-null grid[r][c] has getPosition() equal to (r, c).

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Clears the board and places all 32 pieces in the standard starting position. White occupies ranks 1-2 and Black occupies ranks 7-8.

    • isPathClear

      public boolean isPathClear(Position from, Position to)
      Checks whether every square strictly between two positions is empty. The endpoints themselves are not examined.

      Only meaningful for moves along a rank, file, or diagonal. Adjacent squares have no squares between them, so the path is trivially clear.

      Parameters:
      from - starting square
      to - ending square
      Returns:
      true if no piece sits between from and to; false if a piece blocks the path or the squares are not on a common line

    • movePiece

      public Piece movePiece(Position from, Position to)
      Moves a piece, assuming the move has already been validated by the caller.

      Steps, in order: record any captured piece, clear the source square, put the moving piece on the destination square, and update the moving piece's own position so the board invariant still holds.

      Parameters:
      from - square of the piece being moved; must be occupied
      to - destination square
      Returns:
      the captured piece, or null if the destination was empty
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if from is empty
